statement: Let Y be a connected smooth projective variety and let V ⊂ Y be a nonempty connected semialgebraic open subset that is locally pseudoconvex at its boundary. The following data exist, locally at generic centers in totally real parameter boxes. The same assertion holds in smooth projective families with additional real parameters, analytic coefficients, and bounded algebraic fibre data, when the hypotheses hold fibrewise. The constructed data depend analytically on those parameters after generic restriction and may be complexified locally. There is a complex box B ⊂ Cd, a smooth proper projective family q : Q → B with connected fibres of dimension dim Y − d, and a holomorphic evaluation ev : Q → Y , algebraic with bounded data in the projective variables and of full rank on a coordinate patch meeting every fibre. Its fibre images Zb = ev(Qb) are irreducible projective varieties of dimension dim Y − d, and Qb → Zb is proper and surjective. If G = ev−1(V ), a component S of q(G) and a relative proper algebraic subset D ⊂ Q satisfy Qb \ Db ⊂ Gb (b ∈ S). (16) 29 The container D is analytic on the full box and proper in every fibre, after shrinking the box. The actual holes Q|S \ G are analytic; their images give precisely Zb \ V and are algebraic in each fibre. The domain S is locally pseudoconvex at its parameter boundary. Its boundary inside B is disjoint from q(G). All stated shrinkings of B may be made before the choice of scales and sequences. There are a fixed interior seed p, real block diagonal matrices Rt(x) tending to zero with polynomial inverse bounds, and a component P of the open kernel of St,x = Rt(x)−1 (S − x) at p. A fixed neighborhood of p is eventually in St,x. The domain P is a finite recursive tower, beginning at a point and adding a block (s, w) ∈ C × Cr over a previously constructed domain P2 by the condition z ∈ P2, ℑM(s, w, z) > 0, M(s, w, z) = s wT w τ(z) ! , (17) where τ is symmetric and polynomial holomorphic and ℑτ > 0 on P2. For each bounded real u-box the ratios Rt(x)−1 Rt(x + Rt(x)u) −→ Gx(u) (18) converge with every derivative. The matrix Gx is polynomial and block diagonal, each block depends only on later block coordinates, Gx(0) = I, and every block has determinant one. Its inverse is polynomial. For all sufficiently small real u, Z 7−→ u + Gx(u)Z (19) is an automorphism of P. Finally the bounded-path localization conclusion holds: any limit of endpoints of paths in St,x starting at the seed and staying in a fixed bounded box belongs to P. Equivalently, on each fixed bounded box the accessible components have outer distance to P tending to zero.
